questions.stem: Find all values of \(\theta\) satisfying \(\sqrt3\cos\theta=\sin(2\theta)\).
questions.hint: Rewrite \(\sin2\theta\) as \(2\sin\theta\cos\theta\), factor, and solve both factors to obtain all repeating angle families.

keyPoints.note: Keep every factor after factoring; each may give its own family of roots.
Use the double-angle identity before solving.

steps.explain: Use the double-angle identity and collect terms.
Solve the first factor. Cosine is zero at 90° and repeats every 180°.
Solve the second factor. Sine is √3/2 in quadrants I and II.
Combine both families. The unit circle shows the representative angles from each factor.

questions.solution: Correct answer: \(90^\circ+180^\circ k,\ 60^\circ+360^\circ k,\ 120^\circ+360^\circ k;\ k\in\mathbb Z\).

questions.stem: Use the identity in part (i) to help solve the equation in part (ii).
questions.hint: Work through each part in order. Use the identity highlighted in that part, and check the stated interval before selecting every solution.

parts.hint: Write \(\sin3x=\sin(2x+x)\), expand, and use the double-angle identities to collect terms.

keyPoints.note: Start from the left side and transform it until it matches the right side.
Expand the triple angle as \(\sin(2x+x)\).

parts.answer:
Sample answer:
\(\sin x+\sin3x=\sin x+\sin(2x+x)\)
\(=\sin x+\sin2x\cos x+\cos2x\sin x\)
\(=\sin x+2\sin x\cos^2x+(\cos^2x-\sin^2x)\sin x\)
\(=\sin x+3\sin x\cos^2x-\sin^3x\)
\(=\sin x+3\sin x(1-\sin^2x)-\sin^3x\)
\(=4\sin x(1-\sin^2x)=4\sin x\cos^2x=2\sin2x\cos x.\)
parts.solution:
Sample answer:
\(\sin x+\sin3x=\sin x+\sin(2x+x)\)
\(=\sin x+\sin2x\cos x+\cos2x\sin x\)
\(=\sin x+2\sin x\cos^2x+(\cos^2x-\sin^2x)\sin x\)
\(=\sin x+3\sin x\cos^2x-\sin^3x\)
\(=\sin x+3\sin x(1-\sin^2x)-\sin^3x\)
\(=4\sin x(1-\sin^2x)=4\sin x\cos^2x=2\sin2x\cos x.\)

steps.explain: Use the sine addition identity to expand sin(2x+x).
Replace the double-angle terms by sine and cosine products.
Collect terms and use \(\sin^2x+\cos^2x=1\).
Replace 1−sin²x by cos²x and apply sin2x=2sinx cosx.

parts.stem: Hence find all \(x\) satisfying \(\sin x+\sin2x+\sin3x=0\), for \(x\in[0,2\pi]\).
parts.hint: Use part (i) to combine sin x and sin 3x, then factor and solve both factors in the closed interval.

keyPoints.note: Include both endpoints and list any repeated root only once.
Combine the first and third terms using part (i).

steps.explain: Apply part (i) to the first and third terms, then factor out sin 2x.
Solve the first factor over 0≤2x≤4π.
Solve the second factor using the reference angle for cosine −1/2.
Combine both sets without duplicates. The diagram marks the five sine-zero roots and the two extra cosine roots.

questions.stem: Given \(\sin3\theta=3\sin\theta-4\sin^3\theta\), solve \(\sin3\theta+\sin2\theta=\sin\theta\) for \(0\le\theta\le2\pi\). (Do not prove the given identity.)
questions.hint: Substitute the given triple-angle identity and \(\sin2\theta=2\sin\theta\cos\theta\). Factor fully and solve each factor in the closed interval.

keyPoints.text: Do not prove the given identity
keyPoints.note: Use it as a supplied result; focus on solving the equation.
Include both endpoints if they satisfy the original equation.

steps.explain: Substitute both the supplied triple-angle identity and the double-angle identity.
Move all terms to one side and factor out 2 sin θ.
Use sin²θ=1−cos²θ, then factor the quadratic in cosine.
Solve each factor. The cos θ=−1 root θ=π is already in the sin θ=0 set, so do not list it twice.

questions.stem: A billboard of height \(a\) metres is mounted on a building with its bottom edge \(h\) metres above street level. From point P, \(x\) metres from the building, it subtends an angle \(\theta\). Use \(\tan(A-B)=\frac{\tan A-\tan B}{1+\tan A\tan B}\) to show that \(\theta=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{ax}{x^2+h(a+h)}\right)\).

questions.stem: Solve \(\sin7x+\sin x=\sin4x\) for \(0\le x\le\frac{\pi}{2}\).
questions.hint: Use sin A + sin B = 2 sin((A+B)/2) cos((A−B)/2) on the left, then factor out sin 4x.

steps.explain: Use sums to products.
Bring everything to one side and factorise (don't divide by \(\sin4x\) — you would lose solutions).
\(\sin4x=0\) with \(0\le4x\le2\pi\).
\(\cos3x=\frac12\) with \(0\le3x\le\frac{3\pi}{2}\).
All solutions:

keyPoints.note: Sums to products: sin 7x + sin x = 2 sin 4x cos 3x. Factor, don't divide.

parts.stem: Prove the trigonometric identity \(\tan3\theta=\frac{3\tan\theta-\tan^3\theta}{1-3\tan^2\theta}\) using the compound angle formula.
parts.hint: tan 3θ = tan(2θ + θ), then use the tan 2θ formula.

steps.explain: Write \(3\theta=2\theta+\theta\) and use the compound angle formula.
Let \(t=\tan\theta\) and use \(\tan2\theta=\frac{2t}{1-t^2}\).
Multiply numerator and denominator by \(1-t^2\).
Simplify.

parts.answer: \(\tan3\theta=\tan(2\theta+\theta)=\frac{\tan2\theta+\tan\theta}{1-\tan2\theta\tan\theta}\); substitute \(\tan2\theta=\frac{2t}{1-t^2}\) (t = tan θ) and multiply top and bottom by \(1-t^2\): \(\frac{2t+t(1-t^2)}{1-t^2-2t^2}=\frac{3t-t^3}{1-3t^2}\).

keyPoints.note: Split 3θ = 2θ + θ.

parts.stem: Hence find expressions for the exact values of the solutions to the equation \(\frac{3x-x^3}{1-3x^2}=\sqrt3\).
parts.hint: Put x = tan θ so the equation is tan 3θ = √3.

steps.explain: Let \(x=\tan\theta\). By (i) the left side is \(\tan3\theta\).
\(\tan\) has period \(\pi\): \(3\theta=\frac\pi3+k\pi\).
These give three different values of \(\tan\theta\) (a cubic has at most three roots).

keyPoints.note: With x = tan θ, the left side is tan 3θ by part (i).

parts.hint: Turn the equation into a cubic and use the product of roots.

steps.explain: Rearrange the equation into a cubic.
Its three roots are the values from (ii).
Product of the roots of \(ax^3+bx^2+cx+d\) is \(-\frac da\).

parts.answer: \(\frac{3x-x^3}{1-3x^2}=\sqrt3\Rightarrow3x-x^3=\sqrt3-3\sqrt3x^2\Rightarrow x^3-3\sqrt3x^2-3x+\sqrt3=0\). Its roots are the three values from (ii), so their product is \(-\frac da=-\sqrt3\).

keyPoints.note: The three tangents are the roots of the cubic from (ii).

topics.title: The sum of sine and cosine functions

questions.stem: Consider \(3\sin x+4\cos x\).
questions.hint: Work through each part in order. Use the identity highlighted in that part, and check the stated interval before selecting every solution.

parts.stem: Express \(3\sin x+4\cos x\) in the form \(A\sin(x+\alpha)\), where \(0\le\alpha\le\frac\pi2\).
parts.hint: Expand the target form and match the coefficients of sine and cosine separately.

keyPoints.note: Use \(A\sin(x+\alpha)=A\cos\alpha\sin x+A\sin\alpha\cos x\).
Match the sine coefficient to 3 and the cosine coefficient to 4.

steps.explain: Expand the target form using the sine addition identity.
Match the two coefficients.
Square and add, using \(\sin^2\alpha+\cos^2\alpha=1\), to find the positive amplitude.
Both sine and cosine of α are positive, so α is in quadrant I and satisfies the required range.

parts.stem: Hence solve \(3\sin x+4\cos x=5\) for \(0\le x\le2\pi\), giving your answer to two decimal places.
parts.hint: Use the phase form from part (i). Sine equals 1 at \(\frac\pi2+2k\pi\); then keep only values in the original interval.

keyPoints.note: Check the interval after solving for the shifted angle.
Substitute the equivalent sine form from part (i).

steps.explain: Replace the left side with the amplitude-phase form and divide by 5.
In the allowed shifted-angle range, the only angle with sine 1 is π/2.
Round to two decimal places and check the closed interval.

questions.stem: The current in an electrical circuit is modelled by \(f(t)=6\sin(0.05t)+8\cos(0.05t)\), for \(t\ge0\).
questions.hint: Work through each part in order. Use the identity highlighted in that part, and check the stated interval before selecting every solution.

parts.stem: Given \(f(t)=6\sin(0.05t)+8\cos(0.05t)\), express \(f(t)\) in the form \(A\sin(0.05t+b)\), where \(0\le b\le\frac\pi2\).
parts.hint: Expand the phase form, match coefficients, then use \(A=\sqrt{6^2+8^2}\).

keyPoints.note: The coefficients become \(A\cos b\) and \(A\sin b\).
Both coefficients are positive, so b lies in quadrant I.

steps.explain: Expand the requested form and match coefficients.
steps.work: \(A\sin(0.05t+b)=A\cos b\sin(0.05t)+A\sin b\cos(0.05t)\Rightarrow A\cos b=6,\ A\sin b=8\)

steps.explain: Square and add to find A. Divide coefficient equations to find b.
The signs place b in quadrant I, agreeing with the given restriction.

parts.stem: Using part (i), when does the current first reach its maximum value?
parts.hint: A sine function reaches a maximum when its angle is \(\pi/2\). Solve for t and divide by 0.05.

keyPoints.note: Choose the earliest non-negative solution, not a later cycle.
Set the phase angle in the transformed form to its first maximum value.

steps.explain: The first maximum occurs when the sine factor is 1.
Subtract the phase and divide by the coefficient of t.
Round to one decimal place.

parts.stem: Sketch \(f(t)\). Clearly show its range and label the coordinates of its first maximum. Do not label the x-intercepts.

parts.hint: The amplitude gives the range. Use the first-maximum time from part (ii), and start the curve at the value f(0).

questions.stem: By making the substitution \(t=\tan\frac\theta2\), or otherwise, show that \(\csc\theta+\cot\theta=\cot\frac\theta2\).
questions.hint: Use the half-angle expressions for sine and cosine in terms of t, then combine the two fractions. Recall that cot(θ/2)=1/t.

keyPoints.note: Use the standard half-angle expressions for sine and cosine.
Write both terms over the common denominator sin θ.

questions.answer:
Sample answer:
Let \(t=\tan(\theta/2)\). Then
\(\sin\theta=\frac{2t}{1+t^2},\quad \cos\theta=\frac{1-t^2}{1+t^2}\).
Hence
\(\csc\theta+\cot\theta=\frac{1+\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}
=\frac{1+\frac{1-t^2}{1+t^2}}{\frac{2t}{1+t^2}}
=\frac1t=\cot(\theta/2)\),
where the expressions are defined.
